        type:

          format: uri

          readOnly: true

          format: date-time

      properties:
        firstName:

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. It is normalized to E.164 form:
            an explicit leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise country
            code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the
            result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address

            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must be

          type: string

          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'

          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'

## Summary

The codebase already had a partial `sharesHousehold` feature (the create endpoint *skipped* the duplicate-household conflict when the flag was set). The change was to make it also **assign a stable shared `householdId`** and return it.

**New behavior:** when `POST /api/owners` is called with `sharesHousehold: true` and an existing same-last-name owner already occupies that address, the new owner and every existing member of that household are assigned one stable, shared `householdId`, which is then returned on the owner.

### Changes

- **`HouseholdIdGenerator`** (new component, `service/`) — single responsibility: derive a stable, shared household identifier from a last name + address. It normalizes both (trim, collapse whitespace, lower-case) and hashes them (SHA-256 → `HH-<12 hex>`), so any two owners in the same household deterministically map to the same id, independently and across requests. Mirrors the existing `CustomerCodeGenerator` style.

- **`ClinicServiceImpl`** — injected the generator and centralized the normalization there (removed the now-duplicate private `normalizeIdentity`). Added a private `householdMembers(...)` helper reused by both:
  - `existsOwnerByLastNameAndAddress` (the conflict check) — now expressed via `householdMembers`.
  - `shareHousehold(owner)` (new, `@Transactional`) — computes the shared id, backfills it onto existing members that lack it, sets it on the new owner, and returns it.

- **`ClinicService`** — declared the new `shareHousehold` method.

- **`OwnerRestControllerV1`** — on create, when `sharesHousehold` is true it calls `clinicService.shareHousehold(owner)` before saving (each request still takes exactly one path — conflict check *or* household join).

- **`Owner` model** — added the `householdId` field (`household_id` column) with accessors.

- **`openapi.yml`** — added the read-only `householdId` property to the `Owner` schema, so it's mapped (MapStruct auto-maps it) and returned by `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

- **Schema DDL** — added the `household_id` column to all four dialects (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres).

`AcceptanceTest.coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` and the full suite are green.
